title: mail-server: resolve #creationId in /set update keys, destroy ids and /get ids from earlier calls
description: Found during JMAP-tna1.8. RFC 8620 §5.3: the server keeps a creation-id map for the request 'so it can substitute in the correct value if necessary in later method calls'. jmap-mail-server resolves #creationId in Id-typed property values (mailboxIds, parentId, emailId, identityId, and now blobIds) but not in an update key, a destroy id or a /get ids entry: e.g. SieveScript/set update {"#s": ...} after an earlier SieveScript/set created s fails invalidProperties [id] ('Id contains invalid character #'); Email/get ids ["#ok"] after Email/import is notFound-or-error. Parse sites: mailbox.rs, email.rs, sieve.rs parse_wire_id(&id_str, "id"). Check whether jmap-server already offers a shared helper and whether siblings share the gap (blob-server resolves them, design blobext.md table row 'RFC 8620 §5.3 #creationId in update keys / destroy ids'). Decide whether RFC 8620 requires it for update/destroy keys (the blob-server design says yes) before changing; mail is canonical, siblings follow. Acceptance: dispatcher tests where call 1 creates and call 2 updates/destroys/gets via #cid; unknown #ref keeps today's error.
notes: Decision 2026-11-17: RFC 8620 §5.3 'creates happen before their creation ids are referenced by another create/update/destroy in the same call' — a destroy carries only ids, so destroy ids (and update keys) may be creation ids; implemented for update keys and destroy ids via jmap_server::resolve_set_id_refs (entry: earlier calls; after create phase: same call). /get ids NOT done: RFC 8620 §3.3 limits substitution to 'a create/update', and back-references (§3.7) are the spec's mechanism for /get; adding it would be non-standard behaviour in the reference impl. Unknown #ref keeps today's invalidProperties [id].
close_reason: Mail resolves #creationId update keys and destroy ids (earlier and same call); /get ids out per RFC 8620 §3.3; siblings in tna1.16
